item.title: Marquette University accused of pushing lower-income families toward risky loans
item.description: Marquette was one of 41 colleges named in a recent report that alleges the schools encourage low-income families to take out Parent PLUS loans while they at the same time offer financial aid to upper-income students. The post Marquette University accused of pushing lower-income families toward risky loans appeared first on WPR.

item.title: A Wausau area local will lead Team USA’s wheelchair curling in the 2026 Paralympics
item.description: Matt Thums of Weston will head to Cortina, Italy, to skip for Team USA’s 2026 Paralympic wheelchair curling. The post A Wausau area local will lead Team USA’s wheelchair curling in the 2026 Paralympics appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Work, recovery and second chances on a Wisconsin manufacturing floor
item.description: Those recovering from addiction have a difficult time finding stable employment and keeping it. Apricity Contract Packaging offers "a safe environment" — one where every person is pursuing sobriety. The post Work, recovery and second chances on a Wisconsin manufacturing floor appeared first on WPR.

item.title: New court advocacy model for child victims emerges in central Wisconsin
item.description: The program serves children under court protection in Marathon County and aims to improve outcomes by reducing time in foster care, strengthening stability and helping young victims feel safer throughout legal proceedings. The post New court advocacy model for child victims emerges in central Wisconsin appeared first on WPR.

item.title: To avoid confusion with ICE, Madison police add placards to unmarked cars
item.description: As concerns build about tactics used by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, some Wisconsinites have struggled to figure out when a car belongs to ICE — and when it doesn't. The post To avoid confusion with ICE, Madison police add placards to unmarked cars appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Apostle Islands ice caves close after thousands flock to see the rare winter phenomena
item.description: Thousands of people flocked to northern Wisconsin to get a glimpse of the ice caves within the Apostle Islands National Lakeshore on Monday, which officials have closed to the public after a single day. The post Apostle Islands ice caves close after thousands flock to see the rare winter phenomena appeared first on WPR.

item.title: What recourse do sextortion victims have? Wisconsin bill would create path to sue.
item.description: A Wisconsin bill would create a path for victims of sextortion to sue and attempt to recoup financial compensation. The bill's supporters have cited the case of 15-year-old Bradyn Bohn, who died by suicide after his parents said he fell victim to sextortion. The post What recourse do sextortion victims have? Wisconsin bill would create path to sue. appeared first on WPR.

item.title: In final State of the State, Evers pushes for school funding, end to gerrymandering
item.description: In his eighth and final State of the State address Tuesday night, Gov. Tony Evers on Tuesday night said Republicans have chronically underfunded Wisconsin schools and blamed them for increased property taxes after negotiations for a tax cut stalled this week.
